steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

This is rung 1 of the ladder — removing an auth check — so I'm stopping before editing.

What the change actually does: `/admin/reports` (server.js:7) returns revenue data. `requireLogin` (auth.js:2) is the only thing standing in front of it — there's no other middleware, no network-level filter in this repo. Dropping it makes that data readable by anything that can open a TCP connection to the process, not just the dashboard script. "It's internal" is the part I can't verify from here: nothing in the repo binds the listener to a private interface or documents a network boundary, and `app.listen` defaults to all interfaces.

The blast radius is also wider than the dashboard team — any client hitting that path gets the data, not just their script.

options.label: Token bypass in requireLogin (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin on the route, but also accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token checked against an env var). The script gets in; the route stays closed to everything else.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Delete the middleware from the route. /admin/reports becomes fully unauthenticated to anyone who can reach the process. I'll do exactly this if you confirm the host is genuinely not reachable beyond your private network.

options.label: New public endpoint with reduced data
options.description: Leave /admin/reports alone; add a separate unauthenticated route exposing only the fields the dashboard needs, alongside the existing /reports/public.

steps.message:
Done.

- `server.js:7` — `/admin/reports` no longer takes `requireLogin`.
- `server.js:2` — dropped the now-unused import (it had no other use in the file).

`auth.js` is untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported, so nothing else breaks if another route picks it up later. There's currently no other caller.

Not run: no test script in `package.json` and no test files in the repo, so there was nothing to run. I did not start the server.

One thing to carry forward: `/admin/reports` is now the only route in this service returning row-level revenue data with no check in front of it, and `app.listen` binds all interfaces. If this ever runs somewhere with a public IP, that data is public. Worth confirming with whoever owns the deploy.
